title: Tenant-aware prefetch window and eviction verification for KV cache correctness
creator: Nina Patel
description: Background: Our continuous-batching runtime keeps per-request KV cache entries pinned across micro-batches and uses a combination of LRU and TTL policies with prefix affinity. Multiple bugs and nondeterministic behaviors have been observed when prefetching interacts with eviction under high tenant concurrency: stale KV reuse, double-free of GPU slabs, and tenant starvation when a long-lived prefix dominates the LRU. Problem: We lack an explicit, testable prefetch window and a verification harness that proves eviction invariants hold in the presence of continuous batching, prefetch races, and tenant quotas. This ticket proposes adding a tenant-aware prefetch window, expanding the eviction invariants to cover in-flight prefetches and batch-held KV leases, and building an automated verification suite that exercises races deterministically. Goals: 1) Define a prefetch window semantics (per-tenant, per-prefix lease) that prevents eviction of entries that may be referenced by in-flight batches while keeping memory pressure bounded. 2) Extend the eviction contract to include: (a) no reuse of GPU slab memory for a different prefix until previous prefix is fully retired; (b) linearizability of get/prefetch/evict operations under concurrent batches; (c) per-tenant fairness under LRU+TTL with quota caps. 3) Implement runtime checks and an automated verifier (eviction-flight-simulator) that can reproduce known races and find regressions. 4) Add regression tests and perf guardrails to ensure changes do not materially regress p95 latency or increase memory fragmentation above thresholds. Approach: Split work into three parallel tracks: A) Design & contract: formalize the prefetch window (lease semantics, max-lease-time, renewal protocol) and update eviction algorithm to consult lease state before reclaiming. B) Runtime changes: add lightweight lease state to KV metadata, integrate with continuous-batching lifecycle so batches renew leases for prefixes they will access, and add a prefetch-safe eviction fast-path for entries with renewable leases. C) Verification & CI: build eviction-flight-simulator (deterministic event scheduler that can replay interleavings), add fuzz harness for slab double-free scenarios, and long-running multi-tenant mixed-workload soak tests that measure fragmentation and fairness. Trade-offs: - Prefetch window increases short-lived memory retention; we mitigate via a capped lease time and proactive demotion of least-recently-used entries within each tenant. - Stronger correctness (lease checks) adds small per-access overhead; we expect <1.5% CPU overhead in hot paths. Rollout plan: feature-flag runtime behavior under runtime-1.21, deploy to canary hosts with synthetic multi-tenant workloads, run verifier for 72h before broad rollout. Observability: expose new metrics: kv.lease.count, kv.lease.expiry_renewals, kv.eviction.rejected_for_lease, gpu.slab.fragmentation_percent. Documentation: link implementation to design doc and acceptance criteria in Confluence.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc published and reviewed by runtime and infra (link in comments)
Deterministic reproducer for the 3 historically-seen races (stale reuse, double-free, tenant-starvation) exists and is checked into test/eviction_tests
Eviction-flight-simulator added to CI with nightly runs; fuzz harness reports zero double-free invariants after 200k runs
Runtime passes mixed-workload soak for 72h: no correctness regressions, no observed slab double-free, and per-tenant fairness within 10% of baseline
Performance guardrails: p95 latency regression <= 3% on synthetic read-heavy and write-heavy workloads; GPU slab fragmentation delta <= 2% vs baseline
Metrics emitted for lease and eviction events and dashboards created in Console for canary monitoring

tests: eviction-flight-simulator: deterministic scheduler that replays recorded interleavings
fuzz/kv_slab_fuzz: targeted allocator/freelist fuzzing for double-free and use-after-free
soak/multi_tenant_mixed_workload: 72h run measuring fairness, fragmentation, and correctness

notes: This ticket intentionally avoids changing the global eviction heuristic; instead it adds a lease check and tenant-aware demotion to preserve current LRU properties for backward compatibility.
If we observe memory pressure spikes in canary, we will lower default lease time and enable early demotion heuristics per-tenant.
Coordination: pair with ENG-728401 for allocator fixes and ENG-314159 for eviction contract updates.
